correctness.rationale: For each fixed 0<alpha<1,tau>0, subadditivity verifies the Beurling norm and the GRS property; a weighted geometric series gives the exact positive inverse. Its difference-coordinate marginal is the standard random-walk Green function q^|k|/sqrt(1-t^2), derived from the inhomogeneous three-term recurrence. Strict saddle concavity, Gaussian-window Taylor control and exponentially small tails yield the full relative equivalent and the normalized weak Gaussian coefficient law. The logarithmic exponent follows from arcosh(1/t)~sqrt(2(1-t)). 82 independent finite comparisons passed; no finite check substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The natural, directly measurable quantitative invariant is the weighted inverse norm of a basic two-direction Fourier filter approaching its unique torus zero. Qualitative GRS spectral invariance gives the same spectrum for every weight and only asserts invertibility before the boundary, while the sharp norm has a continuously varying stretched-exponential order and explicit prefactor. The Gaussian weighted-coefficient location identifies where inversion loses stability and why generic norm-controlled bounds are far from sharp. This exact boundary and localization law is mathematically motivated even though the reduction and saddle tools are classical, and no general downstream theorem is asserted.
